subject: Hosted API latency: request for a short-term operational measurement bucket
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@finservco.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@finservco.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency — short-term measurement bucket request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. We ran into a predictable month-end batch over the weekend that produced short, sharp p95 spikes in our Hosted API traffic. The spikes are concentrated in a 2–3 hour window that correlates to our batch reconciliation job and are transient — they don't reflect our steady-state user latency.

We wanted to ask whether Redwood can put those hours into a temporary operational measurement bucket (a short-term carveout) so those scheduled batch windows aren't counted against our p95 commitment while we iterate on a mitigation. Specifically:
- Proposed carveout: 72 hours starting the week of 2026-07-20 (we'll confirm exact UTC window).
- We'll provide sample logs, request IDs, and a manifest of the jobs so you can verify correlation.
- We expect to complete a remediation (workload smoothing + KV cache warming) within that timeframe.

Can you outline the evidence you need, the operational steps from Redwood, and any constraints (e.g., minimum notice, canary checks, rollback triggers) required to approve a temporary measurement bucket?

Appreciate it — Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Platform Operations | FinServCo
elena@finservco.com

Attachment: finserv_latency_samples.csv (CSV, 55KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finservco.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency — short-term measurement bucket request

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the sample file. We can support a short-term operational measurement bucket, but we need to agree on a small set of operational controls so the carveout doesn't open unintended gaps in SLA coverage. High-level proposal from Redwood:

1) Scope & window
- Operational bucket length: 72 hours (matches your ask).
- Exact UTC start/end to be confirmed by you; we need a minimum of 48 hours notice to instrument the bucket on our side.

2) Evidence & verification
- Required from FinServCo: request-id list, sample traces (the CSV you attached is a good start), and a short manifest describing the batch job triggers (Doc link or Drive foler).
- Redwood will run a quick correlation check (matching request ids, temporal overlap) and produce an evidence confirmation PDF.

3) Measurement mechanics
- For the carveout window we will: 1) tag requests that match the manifest as "scheduled-operational-event" and 2) exclude those tagged requests from the p95 calculation for the affected 72-hour interval.
- Outside that window the usual p50/p95 measurement buckets apply (p50: 100ms target; p95: 800ms target for your plan).

4) Safety & rollback
- We will run a canary in the first 6 hours of the window: if the canary path shows >5% error rate or evidence of routing issues we will auto-cancel the carveout and revert to normal measurement.
- Any carveout will be logged in the customer console and in our audit trail for transparency.

5) Credits & commercial impact
- If the carveout is used but we detect misrepresentation of evidence (e.g., unrelated traffic labeled as batch), Redwood reserves the right to deny a credit. We will surface estimated credit calculations up front if an SLO would have been missed outside the carveout.

Next steps: if this approach looks acceptable I'll loop in Ben from commercial to draft a brief mutual action note (1 page) and Aditya to confirm runtime feasibility and exact tagging mechanics.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

---

Hannah / Laura — quick tech confirmation and a couple of edge considerations from runtime:

- Feasibility: We can implement a temporal tag+exclude flow on the measurement pipeline for a pre-specified set of request IDs and time windows. The tagging will be applied at the routing layer and propagated to the metrics aggregator so p50/p95 calc excludes tagged requests. Implementation ETA: 48 hours to schedule and instrument, plus a 6-hour canary window as Hannah suggested.

- Canary & triggers: Canary runs will exercise both the cold-start and hot-cache paths. Note that KV cache warming can move p95 substantially; we'll include a KV-warmup indicator in the canary to validate your remediation. Failure triggers: >5% errors OR sustained p95 delta >2x baseline for more than 30 minutes.

- Auditability: We'll produce an evidence confirmation bundle (PDF) that lists the exact request ids excluded and a SHA256 of the manifest you provide. This is important for commercial and compliance reviews.

- Credits: From product/commercial — if the carveout is approved and the evidence bundle verifies the correlation, we will not count the excluded requests against the SLA; commercial credit calculations will be handled by Ben.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the instrumentation steps and share it in the Drive link once Hannah confirms.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
